performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body:
## Codex review — correctness, performance, and structure

I reviewed this at `53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5`, as a delta from `modular-editors`. My recommendation is **do not fold the W2 consumer flip into #2469 yet**. The resident-program core and parity harness are good groundwork, but the recovery/consumption path has several correctness holes that can make a stale worker generation appear current.

### Blocking correctness findings

1. **[P0] `Resident.generation` is ignored, so an eval can run a stale program after a rejected delta.** [`resolve_payload`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/WorkerServer.re#L411-L435) matches only the key and discards the requested generation. [`handle_sync`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/WorkerServer.re#L856-L882) deliberately retains the old resident on `RosterMismatch`, `UnknownItem`, or a missing resident. Because Sync(g) and Evaluate(Resident(g)) are FIFO, the eval immediately following a rejected Sync(g) resolves against the previous resident and returns its result as generation g. The generation needs to be part of the resident slot match (`rp.generation == requested_generation`), with evaluation gated until recovery succeeds. Please add the production-shaped test: Full(g1), bad Items(g2) -> NeedResync, Resident(g2) must not evaluate g1.

2. **[P0] Worker restart drops all residency, then the ACK retry reposts only the resident eval.** [`restart_worker`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/WorkerClient.re#L152-L158) creates a blank worker; the retry path then calls only [`post_evaluate`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/WorkerClient.re#L182-L202). A flipped `Resident` request therefore fails with “no resident program”. Worse, `ShadowResidency.mirror` and `last_ds` survive the restart, so an unchanged document need not emit another sync. The residency owner should cache the latest authoritative Full payload, invalidate its mirror on restart, Full-sync the new worker, and only then retry the eval. This needs an ACK-timeout/restart test with a resident request.

3. **[P1] `NeedResync` does not actually resync until a later semantic edit.** [`on_summary`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/ShadowResidency.re#L151-L159) only sets `mirror := None`. If the user stops typing, the worker stays stale indefinitely; the already-queued Resident eval is also unsafe because of finding 1. Cache the latest authoritative root/settings/segment/probes and immediately send Full on a current-generation `NeedResync`; gate eval for that generation until `SyncOk`.

4. **[P1] Disabling the flip does not clear the cache `calc_auto` actually reads.** [`set_flip`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/ShadowResidency.re#L65-L71) clears `DefStatics.slot`, but [`calc_auto`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/haz3lcore/derived/DefStatics.re#L1362-L1385) obtains its previous value from the separate `slots` table. A clamped chain can therefore be reused after toggle-off even though the comments and `Test_PropagateClamp` say it cannot be caught up incrementally. Add a public reset API that clears/evicts the relevant per-document slot and its MRU entry, and test the real `calc_auto` toggle-on/edit/toggle-off path.

5. **[P1] A worker summary is neither made observable to the view nor durable in the actual statics cache.** [`graft_summary`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/ShadowResidency.re#L110-L149) mutates only the module-global `DefStatics.slot`. It dispatches no model action, while [`CodeWithStatics.calculate`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/app/editors/code/CodeWithStatics.re#L178-L223) retains the existing `CachedStatics` on an ordinary post-result calculation. The per-document `DefStatics.slots` table is not updated either, so a later `calc_auto` can overwrite the graft from its ungrafted entry. In effect the promised “next calculate pass” does not rebuild the displayed error/warning IDs. Prefer carrying a generation-tagged resident summary in modeled editor state and dispatching an explicit `ApplyResidentSummary`; if the global cache remains, update the keyed entry atomically too. Add a test that a cross-item error arriving only in a summary changes the rendered/model error IDs without another edit.

6. **[P2] Grafting replaces the full ID lists with only piece-anchored IDs.** The summary retains synthetic errors/warnings only as counts, but lines 135–139 replace `d_error_ids`/`d_warning_ids` outright. That contradicts the comment that stale items keep their synthetic IDs and can change aggregate problem counts/other consumers. Either preserve the old synthetic subset during the graft or make the worker payload sufficient for every flipped consumer.

### Default behavior and architecture

- The PR description says the experiment is off by default, but [`ShadowResidency.enabled`](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/blob/53523318354af9c8678ed20b1e3d4494a6d53be5/src/web/util/ShadowResidency.re#L17) is `true`. Thus every ordinary statics update duplicates derivation and worker messaging even with `__w2flip(false)`. Before folding anything into #2469, default shadow mode off or make it an explicit development/benchmark flag and measure its steady-state cost.
- The recurring failure mode is that ownership is split across `ScratchMode` (sync ordering), `EvalResult` (generation selection), `WorkerClient` (restart), `ShadowResidency` (mirror/recovery), and `DefStatics` (two caches). I would introduce one `ResidentWorker` state machine owning `{worker_epoch, key, synced_generation, pending_full, recovery_state}`. It should expose “sync authoritative program” and “evaluate generation” operations; no caller should be able to post a Resident eval unless that state machine has acknowledged the exact generation. That would eliminate several comments-as-invariants and make restart/resync tests headless.

### What looks solid

The `ResidentProgram` full/delta engine, roster verification, summary parity representation, and loopback tests are a sensible base. I would be comfortable merging that core and its tests independently, but not the consumer flip/recovery wiring above. The missing test matrix is specifically: generation mismatch, rejected-delta eval, worker restart, immediate resync, real `calc_auto` toggle-off, and summary-to-view application.

Validation update: `dune build @src/fmt src --profile dev` passed, and the complete local `@runtest` run passed **3,861 tests in 843.536s** at `5352331`. The findings above are gaps in scenarios the current suite does not exercise, not existing test failures.
